about.text: The Moroccan and Algerian fermented buttermilk. Raw milk is left to sour on its own at room temperature until it sets, then churned to separate raw butter (zebda beldia). The tangy skimmed liquid that remains is lben. It keeps only a few days.

sources.text: The photograph, its author and its licence, from its page.

how.label: ferment, churn
how.text: Lben is the skimmed sour milk left after raw milk soured by wild lactococci, leuconostocs and Lactobacillus plantarum has been churned for butter. Unrefrigerated, it becomes strongly acidic within 2–3 days.
